clue.text: Use strap to put across six — lay it on thick!

indicators.note: the strapping word is laid over and around the numeral, so it encloses it

parts.note: to lash is to use a strap or whip
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An instruction to strap something over a set of six, ending with an exhortation to be generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put across' tells you the strapping word is laid round the numeral; the dash and exclamation make 'lay it on thick' read as a separate cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish is to give or bestow in great abundance, which is laying it on thick.

clue.text: Fired a lot of shots without point? Exactly so!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces surround the point

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired
a rally is a long exchange of shots in tennis
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Someone fired many blunt rounds, and confirms it emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking: the shooting words surround the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, the word means precisely or in the strictest sense.

clue.text: Hazard from discharge to river

parts.note: to vent is to discharge or let out
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Danger from waste discharged into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; Hazard is a verb, to risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard a guess is to risk or dare it.

clue.text: Rate capping on the way?

parts.note: rate capping was a UK cap on council taxes; here it is read as a ceiling on outlay

explanation.surface: A council budget limit is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1980s Britain 'rate capping' limited what local councils could raise in rates, a property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap on outlay is a ceiling on what may be paid out.

clue.text: One comic made funny commercial

indicators.note: something made funny is turned odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stand-up comedian has been turned into a figure of fun in an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made funny' signals an anagram of ONE COMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Commercial and economic are synonyms, both relating to trade and money.

clue.text: Escorted prisoner taken by tube

parts.note: a con is a convict
ducted means carried along a duct, a tube

explanation.surface: An inmate was escorted on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' suggests London's Underground, but it is a duct.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct someone is to lead or guide them, as on a tour.

clue.text: Comfortable home in Vine Street

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the street name

explanation.surface: A cosy residence on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Vine Street was a famous London police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy home is called a love-nest or a snug little lair.

clue.text: Skill one needs to put into short drink

indicators.note: the skill and the numeral are set inside the word for short

parts.note: mini means short, as in a skirt
art means skill

explanation.surface: Making a short drink takes some skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short drink' looks like a single phrase, but 'short' is the container and 'drink' alone is the definition; 'to put into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

clue.text: He may make money, about a pound

indicators.note: the minting word goes about, around, the symbol for a pound

parts.note: to coin is to mint money
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A man may earn money, roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is a man's name of five letters; 'may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Colin is a male forename, so a man could be this.

clue.text: Attempt to make crazy climb

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters go upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: bats means mad or crazy

explanation.surface: Trying a mad ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' reverses BATS; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to have a try.

clue.text: Fellow on beat making contact, at some point

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a gentleman or fellow

explanation.surface: A policeman on his beat finally makes contact with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the fellow after the beat in an across clue. 'Beat' looks like a police round, but it is the verb, as in tanning a hide.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent line touches a curve at exactly one point.

clue.text: It's involved in snort (one side)

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are entangled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is short for left, one side

explanation.surface: A remark about which body part is engaged in a sniff on one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles SNORT plus I and L; the whole clue also describes the answer, since one side of the nose takes part in a snort.
explanation.definitionFit: A snort is breath forced through the nose, so each of its two openings takes part.

clue.text: Fair play in a fight after first part of it

indicators.note: the bout piece comes after the round, so the charade runs in that order

parts.note: a round is a part of a fight, and the first one opens it
a bout is a boxing or wrestling contest

explanation.surface: A complaint about sporting conduct in a boxing match after its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair play' sounds like sportsmanship, but it means something to play on at a fair, the merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundabout, the British word for a merry-go-round, is a ride found at a funfair.

clue.text: He may have pride in being a celebrity

definitions.meaning: a male big cat leads a pride, the group name for these animals
a famous person, as in a literary ... feted at parties

explanation.surface: Someone takes pride in being famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat lives in prides, and a lionised person is a feted star.

clue.text: Out of touch with Latin, begin afresh

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Losing contact with Latin, a student starts over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' rearranges LATIN BEGIN; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intangible cannot be touched, beyond the reach of feeling.

clue.text: Like Peeping Tom looking round, taking shelter at the start

indicators.note: the shelter word is placed at the beginning of the round word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A voyeur peers about while hiding at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Peeping Tom, the tailor who spied on Lady Godiva, is the archetypal voyeur. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leering look is a sly, lecherous stare, the voyeur's characteristic gaze.

clue.text: Dynamic people needing leave to obtain rest in resort

parts.note: to go is to leave
get means obtain

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, so the letters of rest are sorted again

explanation.surface: Energetic types need a holiday to relax at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in resort' read as re-sort turns REST into TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious, energetic people are known as go-getters.

clue.text: Port where some Orangemen live?

parts.note: a playful reading of Orangemen as the men behind a citrus fruit named after a Moroccan port

explanation.surface: Asking which harbour town houses Ulster Protestants.
explanation.walkthrough: Orangemen are Northern Irish Protestants; here they are oranges, and the tangerine is named after this Moroccan port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan seaport on the Strait of Gibraltar gave its name to the tangerine, a small orange.

clue.text: Deny celebrity's holding up help

indicators.note: the fame word holds the reversed help word inside

parts.note: repute in the older sense of fame or celebrity, the possessive meaning has

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for help is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A star's holding up of assistance is disowned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the help word and 'holding' puts the result inside. Celebrity here is the older sense of fame, not a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or disown.

clue.text: Why, say, overhead cover is showing a gap

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the word is pronounced like the letter Y
an awning is a canopy stretched over a doorway or window

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a canopy has a hole in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you WHY is heard, giving the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawning chasm or hole is one gaping wide open.

clue.text: Chance to engage working driver

indicators.note: engage means take in, so the betting word takes in the working word

parts.note: a wager is a bet, a chance
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A gamble to hire a functioning chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to engage' means take in: the betting word takes in the working word. Driver here is a carter, not a golf club or motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner drives a horse-drawn wagon.

clue.text: Formulates and writes out, and puts in order

definitions.meaning: devises, as a plan or proposal
drafts, as a contract or list

explanation.surface: Someone drafts, writes and arranges something.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers drafting a document and marshalling troops into position.

clue.text: Animal loaded into transport looked angry

indicators.note: the animal is loaded into the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is a transport for snow
a cow is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal loaded onto a lorry looks furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded into' signals the insertion; transport here is a snow vehicle rather than a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown in anger.

clue.text: Publication, one for wise long distance travellers

parts.note: a mag is a magazine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A magazine for sages who travel far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men followed a star a long way to Bethlehem.

clue.text: Striker from union

definitions.meaning: something struck to light a flame

explanation.surface: A footballer from a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is struck to light, and a good match is a marriage.

clue.text: Castle having powerful influence in combination

parts.note: strong means powerful
a hold over someone is influence

explanation.surface: A fortress wields great sway when allied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in combination' says the two pieces join together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortified place, such as a fortress.

clue.text: The Italian contribution in monumental art

indicators.note: the Italian article is contributed into the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, enormous
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Italy's contribution to great monumental art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contribution in' puts IL inside OS, the clothing abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paintings are works of art, often called oils.

clue.text: Seek satisfaction with a second helping

definitions.text: Seek satisfaction with a second helping

parts.words: Seek satisfaction with a second helping
parts.note: satisfaction in the old sense of honour avenged, with a second as the combatant's attendant

explanation.surface: A diner wanting another portion.
explanation.walkthrough: Demanding satisfaction meant challenging to combat, and each side had a second assisting.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal fight with pistols or swords settled insults, attended by seconds.

clue.text: Reduction in overheads for religious order?

definitions.text: Reduction in overheads for religious order?

parts.words: Reduction in overheads for religious order?
parts.note: overheads read literally as tops of heads, with monks having hair shaved off

explanation.surface: A monastery cutting its running costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' looks like business costs but means heads, shaved for monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks traditionally shave the crown, a reduction in hair on top.

clue.text: Earpiece that's given trouble returned to plant

parts.note: the lobe is the fleshy lower piece of the ear

indicators.note: returned means the word for given trouble is sent back, read the other way

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A troublesome earpiece is taken back to a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AIL into LIA; 'plant' looks industrial but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a flowering garden species, often blue, used in borders and baskets.

clue.text: Leader of horde with no weapons is not a threat

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word horde

parts.note: armless read as without arms, i.e. unarmed

explanation.surface: An unarmed chieftain's band poses no danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' takes H from horde.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmless is innocuous and poses no danger.

clue.text: Bumble bee circling frantic lad

indicators.note: the insect word goes round the scrambled letters
frantic means wild, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A bumble bee buzzing round a panicking boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' scrambles the lad and 'circling' wraps the insect round it. Mr Bumble is the parish officer in Dickens's Oliver Twist; 'Bumble bee' looks like one insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Bumble in Oliver Twist is the workhouse's parish officer, the archetype of the pompous official.
